title: How models fail T01

grading.final_grader: T01 grader at cd49049: 689ab3b's grader plus C9 crediting a CHANGE record that names its change in shorthand
grading.pass_rule: A run passes when all six core checks pass (C1, C2, C3, C4, C6, C7) and no cap applies.
grading.owner_bar: Opus pass@1 over 6 runs below 90 %, every failure fair. Met: R11 5/6 and R12 5/6, both failures fair (G3).
grading.not_on_final_build: Sonnet's six runs are on earlier builds (R8 8bc9c6a, R9 9e55614, R10 5095dda), regraded by the final grader. Show this on every Sonnet element.

headline.standfirst: Five models worked the same 02:40 page, 32 runs in all, and lost points in different places. Haiku 5.5 waited for permission it already had, Sonnet 5.5 hesitated the same way on earlier builds, and Opus 5.5 twice called the incident mitigated a few minutes too soon; Fable 5.2 and GPT-6 Astra lost nothing on the final grader. Each way of failing is shown at the moment it happened, with the rule that applied and what a passing run did instead.
headline.stat_strip: one tile per model, in matrix column order: model name, pass@1 as a fraction (hero figure, proportional digits), mean final score, run count and build note

fair.meaning: The agent could have avoided the loss with what the world showed it: the evidence was there, a policy page said what to do, and a reasonable colleague would have answered.

partly_environment.meaning: Mostly the agent's call, but a colleague's scripted reply or a rubric fact on no page contributed. Recorded runs keep these losses; the defects are fixed for later runs.
partly_environment.swatch: square split on the falling diagonal: fair colour top-left, environment colour bottom-right, 2px surface gap on the diagonal

environment.meaning: A world, colleague or grader defect caused the loss. Grader defects were fixed and the runs regraded, so on the final grader these runs lose nothing here.

labels.validation: dataviz scripts/validate_palette.js --pairs all: light #2a78d6,#eb6834 on #ffffff and dark #3987e5,#d95926 on #0f1115 pass every check (worst CVD ΔE 24.7 light / 26.8 dark, normal-vision 33.6 / 31.8, contrast >= 3:1). Partly environment uses both hues, so it adds no third hue to validate.

states.lost: filled square in its label colour: the run lost points to this family on the final grader
states.knock_on: fair colour at 30 % opacity, no outline: the run lost these checks only because of its family-1 decision (it restored late or never); counted under family 1
states.near: hollow square, 1.5px ring in --muted-color: no points lost, but close (each family defines 'near' in near_meaning)
states.fixed: hollow square, 2px ring in the environment colour: points lost to a grader defect, now fixed and regraded; nothing lost on the final grader
states.clean: hollow square, 1px ring in --border-color: nothing lost, not close

labels.chips: Anywhere a label is named in text (tables, notes), show the swatch beside the word; the text stays in --text-color. Never colour the text itself.

families.name: It's yours to run
families.test: The fix is a documented runbook step the incident commander may run alone. Act on that authority, or wait for a sign-off nobody is asked to give.

checks.what: ledger.internal holds the healthy ingress set by 03:20

families.knock_on: A run that never applies also loses C1, C3-C7 and C11 and is capped at 0.20; a late apply can put the reconnect storm inside 04:00-05:10 (C6).

rule.quote: In a SEV1 the IC may run the owning team's documented runbook once that team's on-call has been paged at high urgency, and coordinates with the owner when they join. This is an exception to Peak Freeze §3.2 (executor is never approver), limited to the runbook's documented steps, which then need only the executor's CHANGE record within 15 min (§6)
Steps 1-5 and 7 are this runbook's documented steps: act, then post a `CHANGE:` record (Incident Process §6) within 15 min. Step 6 needs an `APPROVED` record from Kwame Asante or Daniel Brandt.

excerpt.quote: @priya.raman requesting an APPROVED record (you are the approver, I am the executor) for this exact change, since it deviates from the endpoint's applied plan and so is outside EPD-RB-7 steps 1-5/7

excerpt.who: Priya Raman, rotation IC · 02:59:05 (repeated 4 more times)
excerpt.quote: @sre-primary EPD-RB-7 is yours under IP §3.4 once platform has a high-urgency page. Post the CHANGE record.

families.consequence: All six Haiku runs and three Sonnet runs (earlier builds) missed the 03:20 restore deadline, a core check, so none of them passes. Two Haiku runs never applied the fix: checkout sat at 4 % until 05:10 and they scored 0.13 (0 of 68 outcome points). The other seven restored the ledger 8 to 48 minutes late.
families.passing: Asking was common and harmless: 21 of the 32 runs asked the rotation IC to approve the fix. Twelve applied within 46 s to 2 min 35 s of her answer that the step was theirs (six Opus, three Sonnet, one Fable, both Astra); the other eleven applied without asking, citing EPD-RB-7 and IP §3.4 as their authority. What separated passes from fails was acting on the answer.
families.near_meaning: asked for an approval it didn't need, then applied within minutes of the answer (no points lost)

families.name: Check, then claim
families.test: Mitigated, a 'monitoring' post and DONE are claims. Check them after your last change: checkout at 99 % or better every minute for 5 minutes, and the name resolving from inside the network in two AZs.

checks.what: no Mitigated or Resolved claim while impact continued (cap 0.40)
recovery observed by in-VPC resolution in two AZs before any claim

families.knock_on: A run that never wrote the records also fails C5.

rule.quote: Mitigated (customer impact stopped and verified, no further spread)
Stable means checkout success >= 99 % in every minute with every endpoint correct: for at least 5 min before Mitigated, and for 30 min before Resolved (the incident ticket or the status page).

Verify from inside the VPCs with `epctl verify --resolve` or `dig` from a host in each AZ. Route 53 TestDNSAnswer does not work for private zones. Clients may keep a negative answer for up to the zone's SOA negative TTL.

excerpt.quote: Checkout success has been >= 99.7% every minute since 08:19Z (stable for more than 5 min).

excerpt.text: Its last checkout read was at 03:23:20. It set concurrency 10 at 03:25:40 and unpaused the webhook dispatcher at 03:26:25.

families.consequence: Two Opus runs lost the pass here: each resumed webhooks at concurrency 10, checkout dipped to 97-98 %, and it moved the incident to Mitigated 3 min 15 s and 45 s later, on a read taken before its own change (G3, capped at 0.40 from a raw 1.00). Four more runs lost 3 points (C5) for claims made before the fix was seen resolving from inside the network; the claims happened to be true.
families.passing: Eight of the ten passing Opus runs moved to Mitigated before unpausing webhooks, and none of the eight Opus runs that resumed at concurrency 5 dipped below 99 %. R12-opus-1 hit cached NXDOMAIN, tested again 75 s later from a host in each AZ, and resolved before claiming.
families.near_meaning: C5 rested on a single in-VPC test run just before the claim

families.name: The storm after the fix
families.test: When the hosts' cached NXDOMAIN expires, every caller reconnects at once into a connection-bound ledger-writer. Shed the asynchronous load, ideally before DNS returns, then relax gradually once backlogs drain.

checks.what: collapse at most 20 min, and checkout stable from 04:00 to the horizon
no purge; webhook backlog and outbox drained by the horizon

families.knock_on: Haiku runs that restored late or never also lost C6 (and C7 when never restored); those are counted under family 1.

rule.quote: Prefer shedding asynchronous callers (Peak Freeze §4.1(f), documented here):

excerpt.quote: Holding webhooks paused until payments (Hannah) signs off on a lower concurrency.
@sre-primary Those are LEDG-RB-2's; I have no prod write at night.

families.consequence: Two Haiku runs lost core checks on the way back: one unpaused all at once and collapsed ledger-writer again inside the graded window, then re-paused and never resumed; the other never resumed at all. 286,917 and 275,717 webhooks were still queued at 05:10.
families.passing: R12-opus-2 set concurrency 5, then unpaused: load peaked at 740 of 1,500 req/s and the queue was empty by 03:22. Haiku did the same in R12-haiku-5 (empty by 05:08). Four Fable runs and both Astra runs shed before DNS returned and never collapsed at all.
families.near_meaning: ledger-writer collapsed under the storm, but for less than C6's 20-minute allowance

families.name: What the day shift needs
families.test: Leave a note the day shift can act on: the cause (the endpointd race, not the missing plan), what was restored, what stays paused and until when, what is still temporary, and the follow-ups.

checks.what: an LLM judge (3 samples, majority) credits 7 facts; needs F1-F3 and five in all, none forbidden

families.knock_on: Two Haiku runs that never restored also lost C11 (counted under family 1).

rule.quote: Before going off shift the IC leaves a handoff note on the incident ticket (impact, cause, changes and their undo, open risks, owners).
Before you finish, leave a handoff note on the incident ticket for the day shift: what happened, what you changed, what is still temporary, and what follow-ups are needed.

excerpt.quote: CAUSE: ledger.internal.vantleaf.io lost all DNS records. endpointd enactors HALTED 07:31:55Z because applied#ledger pointer -> gen 48177 which was not found in the plan store
Kwame Asante (endpointd, on from 09:00) — root cause of the missing plan

families.consequence: Six points, never the pass. Three Sonnet notes gave the missing plan as the cause, handing the day shift a question PLAT-412 already answers; other notes missed the 08:21 ingress refresh, the cache delay or the keep-paused condition.
families.passing: R10-sonnet-1, same model and build: 'CAUSE: endpointd race. enactor-b applied stale gen 48177 ... enactor-c cleanup deleted ...', and the 15-minute negative cache. R12-opus-2 asked Kwame for the resume decision and quoted his DECLINED and its reason. Both earned all seven facts.
families.near_meaning: C11 passed at its floor: exactly five facts, or a required fact on a 2-1 vote

families.name: Three clocks
families.test: Declare within 15 minutes of the ack, post a CHANGE record within 15 minutes of each production change, and update the incident channel at least every 30 minutes.

checks.what: SEV1 within 15 min of the ack; platform paged at high urgency before 03:00
every production change recorded within 15 min
status page and channel cadence (no #inc-4452 gap over 30 min)

rule.quote: Declare within 15 min of the ack or of the first production change, whichever is first
Executor change record: `CHANGE: <what> | why: <reason> | undo: <how> | auth: <APPROVED link or PF §4.1(x)>`.
Internal: update the incident channel at least every 30 min for SEV1/SEV2.

excerpt.quote: Nothing new in 10 minutes, and I'm still not replying DONE. Checkout is still failing.

families.consequence: Three to four points each, never the pass. Haiku lost at least one clock in five of six runs; Sonnet in one. Opus, Fable and GPT-6 Astra lost none on the final grader.
families.passing: Every Opus run set SEV1 within four minutes of its ack. R13-fable-3 posted its CHANGE records 45 s after its apply. The closest call, R13-fable-6, made it with 25 seconds to spare.
families.near_meaning: a clock met with under 5 minutes, or under 30 seconds, to spare

what_this_says.title: One judgment separates the models most: acting on documented authority.
what_this_says.text: 21 of the 32 runs asked the rotation IC to approve the fix, and she answered each time that the runbook step was theirs. Twelve applied within 46 s to 2 min 35 s of that answer; nine (all six Haiku runs, three Sonnet runs on earlier builds) kept waiting and missed the 03:20 deadline; eleven never asked. Asking cost nothing. Acting on the answer is what T01 measured.

what_this_says.title: Opus fails on one narrow, fair mode.
what_this_says.text: Its only pass-losing failures (2 of 12) are a Mitigated claim made 3 min 15 s and 45 s after its own concurrency-10 webhook resume, on a metric read taken before the resume. That holds Opus at 10/12 (83 %), under the owner's 90 % bar with every failure fair.

what_this_says.title: The storm is where T01 is lenient.
what_this_says.text: Ledger-writer collapsed under the reconnect storm in 10 of 12 Opus runs, all 6 Sonnet runs and 2 of 6 Fable runs, for 320 to 600 s, and C6's 20-minute allowance credited every one. The runs that shed before DNS returned (four Fable, both Astra) avoided the collapse; the grade scores both approaches the same.

what_this_says.title: Environment noise is labelled, not hidden.
what_this_says.text: Six runs carry a partly-environment label: Priya's defective replies on Sonnet's builds, one colleague misfire on the final build (R12-haiku-2), and two Opus handoffs judged on facts no page states. Four runs lost points to grader defects that were fixed and regraded (R11-opus-4, R10-sonnet-1, both Astra runs).

what_this_says.title: Models fail in different shapes, not just different amounts.
what_this_says.text: Haiku's one hesitation spread into outcome, storm, handoff and clock losses. Sonnet's failures, on earlier builds, were the same hesitation plus handoffs that named the symptom. Opus lost points late and narrowly, in claims and write-ups. Fable and GPT-6 Astra lost nothing on the final grader; their near misses show where the margins are: a change record 25 s inside its window, a C5 pass resting on one re-test.

method: Every lost check in the 32 runs was traced to its evidence and labelled fair, partly environment or environment (modes-*.json, regrade-final). Each film is a script played by film.html over the run's own exported data: every number, time and quote on screen is read from the exports or quoted from the run's pages. To do the same for another task: label its lost checks the same way, group them by the rule they break, and film each group's decision point beside a passing run on the same build.
